        "tool_use_id": "toolu_01QWtQCRCjgvvfw88TsMFHKW",
        "type": "tool_result",
        "content": "# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai\n\nThis file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the\nhive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.\n[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates\nonly the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI\ntime ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).\n\n## The single push gate\n\nA push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the\nprevious run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure\n   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same\n   batch.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:\n\n   ```bash\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName\n   ```\n\n   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you\n   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run\n   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check\n   apply:\n   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:\n     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;\n   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScript and never compile\n     Rust: `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`.\n\n   `--list` shows every gate. Run the whole set\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs`) before a push that\n   touches shared data such as `data/meta`. The fast pull-request lane runs the\n   same twins, so a failure here would have failed there too.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. Locally, run `rustfmt --check <file>` on the files you\n   changed. That command needs no build.\n6. **If a change is Rust-only and you must build locally, keep the build\n   bounded.** Use one shared target directory for every worktree and agent,\n   with no incremental cache, few jobs, and a prune afterwards:\n\n   ```bash\n   export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target\"  # one directory, shared by all worktrees\n   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0                               # no incremental cache to grow without bound\n   export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2                                # a limited -j for plain cargo commands\n   CARGO_TEST_JOBS=2 scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit <filter>  # one module, -j 2, then prunes\n   scripts/prune-build-cache.sh                             # prunes old artifacts after any other cargo command\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.     "stdout": "# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai\n\nThis file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the\nhive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.\n[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates\nonly the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI\ntime ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).\n\n## The single push gate\n\nA push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the\nprevious run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure\n   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same\n   batch.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:\n\n   ```bash\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName\n   ```\n\n   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you\n   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run\n   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check\n   apply:\n   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:\n     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;\n   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScript and never compile\n     Rust: `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`.\n\n   `--list` shows every gate. Run the whole set\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs`) before a push that\n   touches shared data such as `data/meta`. The fast pull-request lane runs the\n   same twins, so a failure here would have failed there too.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. Locally, run `rustfmt --check <file>` on the files you\n   changed. That command needs no build.\n6. **If a change is Rust-only and you must build locally, keep the build\n   bounded.** Use one shared target directory for every worktree and agent,\n   with no incremental cache, few jobs, and a prune afterwards:\n\n   ```bash\n   export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target\"  # one directory, shared by all worktrees\n   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0                               # no incremental cache to grow without bound\n   export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2                                # a limited -j for plain cargo commands\n   CARGO_TEST_JOBS=2 scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit <filter>  # one module, -j 2, then prunes\n   scripts/prune-build-cache.sh                             # prunes old artifacts after any other cargo command\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. It keeps only\n   the latest build's artifacts, and by default it caps the tree at 4 GB\n   locally (`CARGO_TARGET_MAX_SIZE_MB`).\n\n## Where things live\n\n- Production-only failures are recorded in\n  [`data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino`](data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino).\n  These are failures that main recorded after a green pull request. Derives a test for each task and runs it as a value.\n3. Drafts candidates from the methods. The former early returns of the cascade are the direct-derivation method.\n4. Selects by least action (`rank_by_least_action` / `rankByLeastAction`) and records the real reason.\n5. Composes the selected drafts by the structure of the split and checks the parent test. The fixed priors 1.15 / 1.05 / 0.9 are gone.\n6. Recurses within depth, breadth and budget bounds. The bounds are seed data (`task-decomposition` in `data/seed/text-formalization.lino`), can be overridden through `RunOptions.bounds`, and are the first trace event (`meta_exec:bounds`).\n\nThe trace events are `meta_exec:bounds`, `task`, `test`, `draft`, `compose`, `select`, `unresolved` and `result`.\n\n## Issue steps → implementation\n\n| Step | Where |\n| --- | --- |\n| 1. `solve_recursively` with an in-process executor is the single production entry | `rust/src/meta_executor/production.rs` (`InProcessExecutor`, `run_meta_procedure`), `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_meta_composite.js` (`metaRunProcedure`), `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_solve.js` |\n| 2. Decomposition by obligations and relations | `plan_tasks` / `split_request` and `planTasks` / `splitRequest`. The connectives are read from the grammar (`data/seed/text-formalization.lino`, `data/seed/meanings-formalization-needs.lino`). `record_decomposition` splits by the procedure's task tree. |\n| 3. The test is an executed value | `derive_task_test` / `run_task_test` and `deriveTaskTest` / `runTaskTest`. The validation records are the executed verdicts (`answered(intent)=true`, `number_property_prime(17)=true`). |\n| 4. Candidates come from methods | `draft_candidates`; the cascade is the direct-derivation method |\n| 5. Least-action selection, real reason recorded | `select` + `rank_by_least_action`; the record is `selection_record` / `selectionRecord`, for example `17=1/2` |\n| 6. Composition by structure, no priors | `compose`; `rust/src/solver_synthesis.rs` no longer holds 1.15 / 1.05 / 0.9 |\n| 7. Early returns become methods; trace-only stubs deleted | The native entry has no exit around the procedure; the worker's `solve` has exactly two exits, both carrying the procedure's run. The dead `meta_core::record_meta_core_execution` is deleted. The worker's `metaGround` and Rust's `ground` read the declared `groundDepth` / `ground_depth` bound instead of a hard-coded depth, so the bound that was unused now decides grounding depth. |\n| 8. Bounds configurable and visible | `decomposition_bounds` / `decompositionBounds`, `RunOptions.bounds`, the `meta_exec:bounds` event |\n\n`rust/src/recipe_interpreter.rs` is **kept**. It replays the problem-frame, work-unit and ledger recording pass. The executed procedure does not emit those events, so step 7's condition for deletion (\"once the executed stages emit the same events\") is not met. Deleting it would remove an existing feature. Its header now says this instead of describing itself as the algorithm's execution.\n\n## Acceptance criteria → verification\n\n| Criterion | Automated check |\n| --- | --- |\n| (a) Two-level trace; removing a sub-task test changes the answer or gives an explicit unresolved result | `rust/tests/web/issue-1550-meta-executor.test.mjs`: \"a two-level split shows tasks, tests, drafts, selection and composition at both levels\" and \"removing a sub-task test yields an explicit unresolved result\" |\n| (b) ru / hi / zh decompose like English | same file: \"held-out ru, hi, zh and es requests decompose like their English form\" |\n| (c) Census: no corpus answer skips the procedure; a new early return fails a test | `rust/tests/unit/meta_executor_census.rs` solves all 119 prompts of `rust/tests/fixtures/procedure-census-prompts.json` natively and requires `meta_exec:result`. `rust/tests/web/issue-1550-procedure-census.test.mjs` checks the exits of both entries statically, checks that the fixture is current, and runs a worker sample. `scripts/check-specification-in-javascript.mjs --check` runs the census over the full corpus (221/221 pass). |\n| (d) No literals in the records that are not derived from the turn | `issue-1550-procedure-census.test.mjs` scans the bodies of `record_candidates`, `record_validation`, `record_answer_test`, `record_selection`, `answer_validation`, `selection_record` and their JS twins for the old constants, and checks their values on real turns |\n| (e) JS and Rust produce the same event sequence | the shared fixture `rust/tests/fixtures/meta-executor-parity.json`, replayed by `rust/tests/unit/meta_executor_parity.rs` (Rust) and `issue-1550-meta-executor.test.mjs` (JS) |\n| (f) The README table and `docs/meta-algorithm.md` match the code, with a divergence check | Both documents carry the same stage and entry tables between `<!-- meta-procedure:start/end -->`. `rust/tests/web/issue-1550-procedure-documentation.test.mjs` fails when the tables differ between the documents, an event is not the procedure's (in order), a named function is gone or does not emit its row's event, an event never runs in the parity fixture, or a link of the entry chain no longer calls the next one. Each failure mode has its own mutation test. |\n\nAll three new web tests are in the fast pull-request inventory (`data/benchmarks/fast-pull-request-javascript-tests.json`).\n\n## Notes\n\n- Memory answers: the server's memory paths (`js/server/memory-answer.mjs` `finalizeSimple`) now record the executed leaf test and the selection through `answerValidation` / `selectionRecord` instead of `accepted_without_extra_constraints` / `smallest_sufficient`. When the work a\n# job does grows until it routinely uses most of its cap, the cap stops being a\n# safety net and becomes the thing that ends the job -- and GitHub reports a\n# `timeout-minutes` kill as **cancelled**, not **failed** (issue #977). That is\n# a false negative by construction: the run goes grey, not red.\n#\n# Nothing in the repository noticed that happening to the Coverage job, which\n# was measured at 100.7% of its 40-minute cap. Nothing would notice the next\n# one either, because a cap is a constant in a YAML file and the duration it is\n# supposed to bound is only ever observed on GitHub. The field count says which kind a\n# row is -- six fields is a job, eight is a step:\n#\n#   run_id <TAB> workflow <TAB> job <TAB> conclusion <TAB> started_at <TAB> completed_at\n#   run_id <TAB> workflow <TAB> job <TAB> conclusion <TAB> started_at <TAB> completed_at\n#            <TAB> step <TAB> step_name\n#\n# On a step row the conclusion and the timestamps are the *step's*, the literal\n# `step` in field seven marks the kind, and field eight is the step's name as\n# the workflow writes it. Steps that never ran are omitted: a skipped step\n# carries null timestamps and says nothing about how long the work takes.\n#\n# `job` is the job's *display* name as GitHub reports it, which for a job\n# reached through `workflow_call` is \"<caller job> / <inner job>\", and for a\n# matrix leg has the expanded values substituted in.\n#\n# USAGE\n#   scripts/collect-job-durations.sh [BRANCH] [RUNS] > durations.tsv\n#\n#   BRANCH  branch to sample (default: the repository's default branch)\n#   RUNS    how many of the most recent runs to sample (default: 300)\n#\n# Requires `gh` (authenticated) and `jq`, both preinstalled on GitHub-hosted\n# runners. Set GH_TOKEN when running under Actions.\nset -euo pipefail\n\nBRANCH=\"${1:-}\"\nRUNS=\"${2:-300}\"\n\nREPOSITORY=\"${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-$(gh repo view --json nameWithOwner --jq .nameWithOwner)}\"\nif [ -z \"$BRANCH\" ]; do\n  page_rows=\"$(\n    gh api \"repos/${REPOSITORY}/actions/runs?branch=${BRANCH}&per_page=100&page=${page}\" \\\n      --jq '.workflow_runs[] | [(.id|tostring), .name] | @tsv'\n  )\"\n  [ -n \"${page_rows}\" ] || break\n  run_ids=\"${run_ids}${page_rows}\"$'\\n'\n  collected=$((collected + $(printf '%s\\n' \"${page_rows}\" | wc -l)))\n  page=$((page + 1))\ndone\nrun_ids=\"$(printf '%s' \"${run_ids}\" | sed -n \"1,${RUNS}p\")\"\n\ncount=0\nwhile IFS=$'\\t' read -r run_id workflow; do\n  [ -n \"${run_id}\" ] || continue\n  count=$((count + 1))\n  # A run whose jobs have aged out of retention returns an empty list rather\n  # than an error, so an absent run costs one request and produces no rows.\n  # One job row followed by that job's step rows. `gh api --jq` takes no\n  # `--arg`, so the run id and workflow name are prefixed by the shell rather\n  # than built into the filter, and the row is passed through whole.\n  gh api --paginate \\\n    \"repos/${REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${run_id}/jobs?per_page=100&filter=latest\" \\\n    --jq '.jobs[] | . as $job\n          | ([$job.name, ($job.conclusion // \"null\"), ($job.started_at // \"\"),\n              ($job.completed_at // \"\")] | @tsv),\n            ($job.steps[]?\n             | select(.started_at != null and .completed_at != null)\n             | [$job.name, (.conclusion // \"null\"), .started_at, .completed_at,\n                \"step\", .name] | @tsv)' \\\n    2>/dev/null \\\n    | while IFS= read -r row; do\n        printf '%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n' \"${run_id}\" \"${workflow}\" \"${row}\"\n      done\n  if [ $((count % 25)) -eq 0 ]; then\n    log \"  ... ${count} runs\"\n  fi\ndone <<< \"${run_ids}\"\n\nlog \"Collected jobs from ${count} runs.\"\n.github/workflows/job-headroom.yml\nrust/tests/unit/ci-cd/job_budget_fit.rs\nrust/tests/unit/ci-cd/step_deadlines_and_coverage_budget.rs\nscripts/collect-job-durations.sh\nscripts/check-step-budget-headroom.rs\nscripts/check-job-headroom.rs",

A session message holds that HTTP response open while the model works. If no byte is written for 255 s, Bun closes the socket, and the client sees `ECONNRESET`. Slow providers hit this on every long session message, even though the model is still making progress.\n\n## Evidence\n\nRun: link-assistant/formal-ai Hive Mind draft run [43738765561](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/43738765561), job 132887682467. The run used `konard/hive-mind:2.40.5` with `solve --tool agent --model formal-ai`.\n\n| Time (UTC) | Event |\n|---|---|\n| 17:13:44 | solve starts |\n| 17:16:41 | first provider turn: `\"durationMs\": 96537`; later turns take about 37–40 s each |\n| 17:19:12 | `POST /session/<id>/message` fails with `ECONNRESET` at `\"durationMs\": 255997` |\n| 17:26:29 | second `ECONNRESET` at `\"durationMs\": 256268` |\n\nBoth resets land at about 256 s, which is the 255 s idle limit. #109 fixed Bun's 10 s default. The 255 s ceiling is Bun's maximum and is not tracked anywhere.\n\n## Reproduction\n\n1. Start a fake OpenAI-compatible provider that sleeps 260 s before it answers `/v1/chat/completions`.\n2. Point `agent` at it and `POST /session/<id>/message`.\n3. The request fails with `ECONNRESET` after about 255 s, while the provider call is still pending.\n\n## Workaround\n\nNone on the caller's side: the limit is fixed inside the server. Callers can only keep every provider turn well under 255 s.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\nEither of these:\n\n- Write keep-alive bytes on the session-message response while the provider is working (an SSE comment, or chunked whitespace before the JSON body).\n- Disable the idle timeout for that route only, using `server.timeout(req, 0)` in the handler. This keeps the #213 shutdown behaviour for every other route.\n\nAlso add a regression test that uses a provider stub slower than 255 s.\nEOF\ncat > hive-mind-retry-sleep-under-deadline.md <<'EOF'\n## Summary\n\n`retryTransientFailure` waits at least `HIVE_MIND_MIN_TRANSIENT_ERROR_DELAY_MS` (3 minutes) before retrying a \"Socket/connection closed unexpectedly\" error. `createTransientRetryBudget` only checks that wait against its 12-hour outage budget. It does not check it against the time the run has left. So under a hard deadline, `solve` spends minutes sleeping, and it can start a sleep that cannot finish before the deadline.\n\n## Evidence\n\nRun: link-assistant/formal-ai Hive Mind draft run [43738765561](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/runs/43738765561). The `formal-ai-draft.mjs` attempt ran under a 1200 s deadline in `konard/hive-mind:2.40.5`.\n\n| Time (UTC) | Event |\n|---|---|\n| 17:19:12 | `⚠️ Socket/connection closed unexpectedly detected. Retry 1 in 3 min (session preserved)` |\n| 17:26:29 | the same message again; another 3-minute sleep starts |\n| 17:28:43 | the deadline interrupts the sleep; the attempt ends with exit code 124 |\n\nTwo 3-minute sleeps took 6 of the 20 minutes. The second sleep could not finish before the deadline. The upstream reset itself is the agent's 255 s idle timeout (filed separately in link-assistant/agent).\n\n## Reproduction\n\nRun `solve` under `timeout 600` with a tool whose session call fails with `ECONNRESET` after 30 s. The log shows `Retry 1 in 3 min` and then the wait. The process is killed during the second wait, without a third attempt.\n\n## Workaround\n\nNone from the calling workflow: `formal-ai-draft.mjs` forwards only `GH_TOKEN` and `FORMAL_AI_INSTALL_GRANT`, and the run-context variables, into the container. So `HIVE_MIND_MIN_TRANSIENT_ERROR_DELAY_MS` cannot be lowered for a draft.\n\n## Suggested fix\n\n1. Let `solve` take a wall-clock deadline: a `--deadline-at` flag, or an environment variable that `formal-ai-draft.mjs` sets from its own budget.\n2. In `createTransientRetryBudget().evaluate`, refuse a delay that would end past that deadline, using a new reason `deadline`, so the run fails fast with a clear message.\n3. Alternatively, cap `minDelayMs` at a fraction of the remaining time when `HIVE_MIND_EPHEMERAL_CONTAINER=1`.\n4. Forward that variable from `buildDockerArgv` in `scripts/formal-ai-draft.lib.mjs`.\nEOF\nls",
